papers.summary: Learnable Subspace Projections train the subspaces discarded from frozen language-model weights. Across OPT, Qwen3, and Llama-2 models, the authors report lower perplexity than evaluated compression baselines at matched compression ratios, with the advantage growing at high compression.
papers.relevance: Most direct test here of preserving model quality after low-rank compression, though it optimizes compression after pretraining rather than training weights to become compressible.

evidence.quote: One of the two LSP variants has the lowest perplexity in all 12 model–ratio settings, and the margin grows with the ratio.
All baselines run from their official code with the same calibration data and precision as LSP; SVD baselines are evaluated in factorized form

papers.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression

papers.summary: Derives how GD, simplified Adam, ideal Muon, Shampoo, and a K-FAC model change the emergence and decay of singular modes. Controlled matrix-factorization experiments find markedly different transient effective-rank trajectories despite similar final spectra.
papers.relevance: Addresses how optimizer geometry shapes spectral bias, while leaving open whether those dynamics improve LLM weight compressibility.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws

The stable and effective rank curves therefore mainly differ during the transient phase, while their later agreement reflects the unique full observation target rather than identical optimization dynamics.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Clean approximates SOAP preconditioners with Nyström sketches, and Q-Clean further compresses optimizer states. In LLaMA-1.3B pretraining, the reported optimizer-state memory is 4.48 GB for Clean and 1.28 GB for Q-Clean, versus 5.11 GB for AdamW and 2.80 GB for Muon; Clean reaches AdamW’s final loss in 64 rather than 81 hours.
papers.relevance: Provides unusually concrete quality, optimizer-memory, peak-memory, and time comparisons for memory-efficient LLM pretraining.

evidence.quote: Clean reaches AdamW’s final validation loss in 64 64 of the 81 81 hours of AdamW requirements

papers.title: Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr{ö}m Sketching

papers.summary: Rotated Manifold Optimization incorporates the gauge symmetry of LoRA factors. In matched rank-16 mathematical-reasoning fine-tuning, it reports the lowest validation loss across three model sizes; downstream SFT differences are small relative to seed variation, while its Qwen2.5-3B RL comparison reports higher accuracy than Adam at 1.08× per-step time.
papers.relevance: Directly informs both the geometry and practical optimization of low-rank LLM adapters.

papers.summary: A module-matched LoRA rank sweep studies generalization under label noise on four vision backbones and a 7B language model. The reported second-descent pattern is clearest in vision; in the measured settings, parameter-saving post-peak ranks do not reach module-matched dense fine-tuning risk.
papers.relevance: Connects adapter rank and factorized optimization to noisy-label memorization and generalization, with a dense control.

evidence.quote: We quantify this relation under label noise on four vision backbones and a 7 7 B language model with a module-matched rank sweep (MMRS), which extends past full rank and compares every rank with dense fine-tuning of the same modules, paired by seed.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: FOCUS compresses an agent’s live interaction history by estimating which spans matter for future decisions. Its authors evaluate tool-use and other agent benchmarks and report up to 48% less peak context with up to 8.9 percentage points higher task success than uncompressed execution.
papers.relevance: Potentially useful for context management in a handwritten research-digest agent, but the supplied evidence does not test paper retrieval or relevance ranking.

evidence.quote: We recast context compression as a causal decision preservation problem over discrete interaction units and introduce FOCUS
cutting peak context by up to 48% and dependency by 73% while improving task success by up to 8.9 percentage points over uncompressed execution.

papers.title: FOCUS: Training-Free Decision-Preserving Context Compression for LLM Agents

papers.summary: LionMuon alternates occasional Muon spectral steps with cheaper Lion sign steps, sharing a momentum buffer. The abstract reports lower loss than Muon, AdamW, Lion, and Signum at matched token counts on 124M and 355M models, and less wall-clock time to Muon’s final loss in a four-GPU setting.
papers.relevance: Adds a direct pretraining comparison of spectral optimization against compute, optimizer-state, and distributed communication costs.

evidence.quote: Muon’s compute and communication are paid once per $P$ steps, and the optimizer state is half of AdamW’s.
On 124M and 355M models trained on FineWeb, LionMuon with $P=2$ and $P=5$ reaches a lower loss than Muon, AdamW, Lion and Signum at the same number of tokens.

papers.title: LionMuon: Alternating Spectral and Sign Descent for Efficient Training

limitations: LionMuon’s HTML article was unavailable, so its abstract-level claims could not be checked against experimental tables or controls.
The spectral-dynamics paper validates controlled matrix-factorization models, not LLM compressibility or held-out language-model quality.
The LoRA second-descent evidence is strongest in vision; the supplied passages do not establish the same full curve for the 7B language model.
Clean’s 1.3B comparison used a shortened hyperparameter sweep, and its 13B discussion does not supply matched training-quality results.
FOCUS was not evaluated for research-paper retrieval or relevance ranking; code availability and reproducibility were not independently checked.
